programs.name: Computing Science BSc (Major)
programs.a_level_offer: Three approved A-level subjects; no A-level grade requirement is published (admission is competitive and assessed on predicted grades issued on or after 1 March).
programs.ib_offer: Full IB Diploma, six IB courses of which five are the program's required subjects, no grade below 4; previous competitive diploma scores range from 30-37 points depending on program (no Computing Science-specific figure is published).
programs.ap_offer: No SAT or ACT is required (SAT scores may be used to cover a subject deficiency). Each required subject can be met by US high school course marks from the last three years, by AP results sent as final College Board grades (institution code 0963), or by IB. No minimum AP score is published. Required: English; Mathematics; two of Calculus, Chemistry, Physics or Biology; one further approved subject. Accepted AP exams listed on the equivalencies page include AP Pre-Calculus, Calculus AB/BC, Chemistry, Physics (1 and 2, C) and Computer Science A.
programs.required_subjects: English (Literature & Composition); Mathematics; two of Calculus, Chemistry, Physics, Biology; one further subject from Fine Arts, Humanities, Languages other than English or Math/Sciences. A-levels: Mathematics plus two of Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Further Mathematics or Computing Sciences (BSc Science list).
programs.toefl_note: TOEFL iBT, tests taken on or after 21 Jan 2026 (1-6 scale): overall 4.5 with no band below 4.5. Tests before 21 Jan 2026 (0-120 scale): total 90 with no section below 21. TOEFL Home Edition and TOEFL Essentials are not accepted (Home Edition also not accepted for 2027-2028).
programs.english_note: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0; Duolingo 120 (no integrated subscore below 100); PTE Academic 61 (no skill below 60). Applicants with 3+ years of full-time English-medium education meet the requirement without a test. Some programs (Health Sciences, Education) also need Spoken English; the three programs here do not list it.
programs.notes: International fee not stored: no Fall 2027 figure is published. Per the registrar, the BSc in Computing Science is being raised about 26% to Engineering tuition level for Fall 2027 (https://www.ualberta.ca/en/registrar/costs-tuition-fees/tuition-increases.html); the Fall 2026 cohort calculator lists the generic BSc (Science) at $39,792 per year (https://costcalculator.registrar.ualberta.ca/costcalculator/). Admission averages: BSc Major minimum 70%; Faculty of Science competitive range (3-year trend) low 80s to mid 90s, Canadian high-school percentages (https://www.ualberta.ca/en/admissions/how-to-apply/admission-requirements/competitive-requirements.html). IB route: https://www.ualberta.ca/en/admissions/how-to-apply/ib-students/index.html. A-level route: https://www.ualberta.ca/en/admissions/how-to-apply/international-admission-requirements/international-curricula/gce-british-curriculum/index.html and subjects https://www.ualberta.ca/en/admissions/how-to-apply/international-admission-requirements/international-curricula/gce-british-curriculum/gce-subject-requirements.html. AP route: https://www.ualberta.ca/en/admissions/how-to-apply/international-admission-requirements/international-curricula/united-states.html and https://www.ualberta.ca/en/admissions/how-to-apply/international-admission-requirements/international-course-equivalencies.html. Fall 2027 international application deadline 1 March 2027 (program page, 2026-2027 requirements).

programs.name: Economics BA (Major)
programs.a_level_offer: Three approved A-level subjects from Humanities, Fine Arts and/or Sciences (only one Fine Arts); no A-level grade requirement is published (competitive, assessed on predicted grades issued on or after 1 March).
programs.ib_offer: Full IB Diploma, six IB courses of which five are the program's required subjects, no grade below 4; previous competitive diploma scores range from 30-37 points depending on program (no Economics-specific figure is published).
programs.ap_offer: No SAT or ACT is required (SAT scores may be used to cover a subject deficiency). Each required subject can be met by US high school course marks from the last three years, by AP results sent as final College Board grades (institution code 0963), or by IB. No minimum AP score is published. Required: English (Literature & Composition) plus four further approved subjects (one from Fine Arts, Humanities, Languages or Math/Sciences; three from Humanities, Languages or Math/Sciences); the Economics major also requires Mathematics 30-1 or equivalent (Mathematics 31 recommended). AP Micro/Macro Economics, European/World/US History, Government and Politics, Human Geography and Psychology count in Humanities and Social Sciences.
programs.required_subjects: English (Literature & Composition); Mathematics 30-1 or equivalent for the Economics major (Mathematics 31 recommended); three subjects from Humanities, Languages other than English or Math/Sciences; one from Fine Arts, Humanities, Languages or Math/Sciences.
programs.toefl_note: TOEFL iBT, tests taken on or after 21 Jan 2026 (1-6 scale): overall 4.5 with no band below 4.5. Tests before 21 Jan 2026 (0-120 scale): total 90 with no section below 21. TOEFL Home Edition and TOEFL Essentials are not accepted (Home Edition also not accepted for 2027-2028).
programs.english_note: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0; Duolingo 120 (no integrated subscore below 100); PTE Academic 61 (no skill below 60). Applicants with 3+ years of full-time English-medium education meet the requirement without a test. programs.notes: Fee: $39,232.80 per year (shown rounded) for the Bachelor of Arts, Fall 2026 international cohort, off-campus, from the university cost calculator (https://costcalculator.registrar.ualberta.ca/costcalculator/). It is a Fall 2026 figure: the registrar lists a 5.5% increase for new international undergraduates in Fall 2027 (https://www.ualberta.ca/en/registrar/costs-tuition-fees/tuition-increases.html) but publishes no dollar amount, so expect a higher fee for 2027 entry. Tuition is guaranteed for the program length once admitted. Admission averages: Faculty of Arts competitive range (3-year trend) low to mid 70s, Canadian high-school percentages (https://www.ualberta.ca/en/admissions/how-to-apply/admission-requirements/competitive-requirements.html).
